hook.h1: Security checks fast enough that nobody turns them off
hook.lede: Fennec scans every change in seconds for security bugs, leaked secrets, vulnerable libraries and quantum-weak encryption. One tool, on every laptop and pull request. Your code never leaves.

stake.label: passwords, API keys and tokens detected in code on GitHub in a single year

scene.title: A cloud key on its way to production
scene.setup: A software company, Thursday afternoon. A developer finishes a payment feature for tomorrow’s release. A cloud access key is still pasted in a config file.

without.p: The developer commits. The security scan took minutes, so the team switched it off last month.
The key enters the repository history. The pull request passes a quick review and merges.
The release ships with the key and an unchecked input in the new code.
A customer’s security review asks for scan evidence. The team has none to send.

with.p: The developer commits. Fennec checks the change in seconds and stops the key before it enters history.
On the pull request, Fennec shows only what this branch adds: one unchecked input, with the line.
The developer fixes the input from the finding. The release ships on time.
The customer’s security review gets a standard SARIF report from the release.

end.without: A live key in history, a bug in production.
end.with: A clean release, on schedule, with the evidence.

chapters.h: A scanner fast enough to stay switched on
chapters.p: When a scan takes minutes, developers disable it and bugs ship with the next release. Fennec scans in seconds, runs where developers already work and shows only the issues each change adds. The check stays on, and problems are fixed at the keyboard, where fixing costs least.
points: Runs on every save, commit and pull request
Diff mode shows only what a branch adds
Findings inline in VS Code as developers type
Automatic fixes for supported issues
Terminal review that opens the exact line in your editor

chapters.h: One tool instead of three separate scanners
chapters.p: Many companies buy code, secret and dependency scanning separately, and still cannot say what is in their code. Fennec checks all of it in one pass, plus configuration files and encryption. One tool to roll out, one report to read.
points: Security bugs in your own code, across major languages
Follows untrusted input across files to where it harms
Passwords, keys and tokens stopped before they are committed
Open-source libraries with known vulnerabilities
Risky settings in Docker, Terraform, Nginx and other configs

chapters.h: The crypto inventory banks are now asked for
chapters.p: Banks, defense suppliers and critical infrastructure are being asked where their encryption stands. RSA and elliptic-curve crypto must be replaced on CNSA 2.0 timelines, the US schedule for quantum-safe encryption. Fennec finds every use, scores your readiness and writes the inventory in one run.
points: Finds RSA, DSA, elliptic-curve and Diffie-Hellman use
Migration deadline shown for every finding
Credits quantum-safe algorithms such as ML-KEM and ML-DSA
A readiness percentage you can show the board
Crypto bill of materials (CBOM) in CycloneDX format

chapters.h: Switch without rewriting the rules you trust
chapters.p: Your team has written rules for the scanner it uses today. Fennec reuses them without a rewrite and plugs into the places code is reviewed, from pull requests to any CI pipeline. Even AI coding agents can check their own code before you see it.
points: Existing custom rules reused, no rewrite
GitHub Action and GitHub App for pull request checks
Any CI pipeline, failing builds by severity
MCP server lets AI coding agents check their code
Findings become tracked cases in AutoSecOps

chapters.h: Fewer false alarms, measured on your own code
chapters.p: False alarms teach developers to ignore a scanner. Every Fennec rule is tested in CI against vulnerable code and look-alike safe code. Known false-positive patterns are published, and in the pilot accuracy is measured again on your code, not ours.
points: Each rule must fire on its vulnerable test case
Look-alike safe code must produce zero findings
Rules labeled by tier, so teams tune noise
Baselines split new, recurring and resolved findings
Batch ignore or baseline, previewed before anything changes

chapters.h: Audit and customer evidence without extra work
chapters.p: Software companies face customer security reviews and SOC 2 audits. Banks face strict regulators. AI now writes more of the code, and Fennec checks all of it. The same scans produce the standard reports auditors and customers ask for.
points: Standard SARIF reports, including for GitHub code scanning
JSON output for any tool or pipeline
Audit reports for SOC 2 and customer reviews
Crypto inventory for security reviews

items.p: Automatic fixes cover supported issues. Other findings point to the exact line and data flow, and a developer makes the change.
Code, secret and crypto scans run fully offline. Dependency checks look up the public OSV vulnerability database.
Some rules are heuristic. Fennec labels every rule by tier, publishes its known false-positive patterns and re-measures accuracy on your code.

pilot.title: Three repositories, two weeks, a clear report

steps.p: Choose three repositories that matter. Read-only access is all we need, and we connect them in an hour.
The first full scan runs the day you connect. Developers install nothing.
Every pull request is scanned for two weeks, and we tune the rules with your team.
Real findings, live secrets, dependency risk, crypto readiness and scan times, with accuracy measured on your code.

objections.q: What is Fennec, in one sentence?
objections.a: Fennec is Singularity’s code security scanner: in seconds it checks your code for security bugs, leaked secrets, vulnerable open-source libraries, risky configuration and quantum-weak encryption, on developer laptops, in pull requests and in any CI pipeline.

objections.q: Can Fennec run on-premises or in an air-gapped network?
objections.a: Yes. Fennec runs on your own machines, on macOS, Linux and Windows, and your code never leaves them. An air-gapped install is available. Code, secret and crypto scans run fully offline; only dependency checks look up the public OSV vulnerability database.

objections.q: Who decides what blocks a build and what gets ignored?
objections.a: Your team does. With Fennec you choose which severity fails a build. Accepting a finding takes an in-code note that reviewers see in the pull request, and bulk changes are previewed before anything is written. Automatic fixes apply only when you run them.

objections.q: Will Fennec slow my developers down?
objections.a: No. Fennec scans in seconds, fast enough to run before every commit, and shows only the issues a branch adds rather than the whole backlog. Developers see findings where they already work: the command line, VS Code, pre-commit and pull requests.

objections.q: Won’t it bury my team in false positives?
objections.a: Fennec tests every rule against vulnerable code and against look-alike safe code, which must produce zero findings. Each rule is labeled by tier so you can tune noise, and in the pilot Fennec’s accuracy is measured again on your own code.

close.h: Scan three of your repositories in two weeks
close.p: Pick three repositories and a date. You get real findings, leaked secrets and a crypto readiness score from your own code.
